meta.title: C-Medical: 45% more bookings on the same traffic | Elevate Marketing
meta.description: A Norwegian private clinic group, 1 February to 5 November 2026 against the same days of 2025: 3,734 online bookings against 2,567 on 3.5% more visits. Google Ads, SEO and AI search, every figure and what it does not prove.
meta.ogDescription: Nine months for a private clinic group. 45% more online bookings on 3.5% more visits. Google Ads rebuilt one door at a time, SEO and AI search. Every figure, and what it does not show.

topbar: Case study for private hospitals and clinic groups

hero.lede: A private clinic group for women's health, urology, fertility and orthopaedics, with over 60,000 patient visits a year. We took over its Google Ads on 25 January 2026 and its search presence from 1 February. Nine months on: 3.5% more visits, 45% more online bookings.

chapters.h2: Four things we did. Four things the numbers say.

items.title: The takeover
items.line: On 25 January 2026 we took over a Google Ads account with eleven broad campaigns and a Performance Max campaign that partly bought searches for the clinic's own name. From 30 January we rebuilt it: one campaign per treatment, 47 campaigns with real spend by November. Performance Max was switched off.
items.alt: A hand-drawn floor plan on cream paper with a pencil and brass ruler

items.title: One door per treatment
items.line: Google Ads bookings went from 1,251 to 1,601, up 28%, on 11% more spend. The cost of a booking fell from NOK 1,087 to NOK 946, down 13%. Clicks rose 29% and taps on the phone number 41%. The first fourteen weeks were behind 2025. Since mid-May, 2026 has been ahead in 18 of 20 counted weeks.
items.alt: An empty clinic reception counter in oak and stone with a single eucalyptus stem

items.title: Being found without paying
items.line: From February we did the technical and content work on cmedical.no: around 30 articles, about 150 rewritten meta titles, many pages rewritten, and a new website launched in August. Organic bookings went from 932 to 1,547, up 66%, on 12% more organic visits.
items.alt: A neat stack of printed pages on a pale oak desk with a fountain pen

items.title: Being the answer
items.line: Visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini and Claude went from 623 to 1,313, up 111%, and bookings from those visits from 7 to 28. Small numbers still, and growing every month.
items.alt: Soft morning light through frosted glass panels in a clinic

months.eyebrow: Month by month, the whole website
months.h2: Ahead in every month the tracking was whole.
months.intro: Online bookings from every channel, 2026 in ink against 2025 in grey. Eight of ten months are ahead. The two that are not sit in the tracking fault of 13 July to 23 August, which hid bookings from the ads and the organic figures alike; November is five days old. February was the first month after the takeover, with the rebuilt account still learning, and the website was still ahead.

beyond.note: Revenue figures, not profit, and they leave out what we charge. Phone bookings are in none of them: taps on the phone number rose 41%, and if 46% of calls book and 90% attend, add roughly half again. These multiples depend on the attendance, price and procedure figures the clinic group gave us, which we have not audited.

limits.eyebrow: What this case does not show
limits.h2: Read these before you believe the rest.
items: Attendance. Every figure is an online booking, not a patient in a chair. The 92% attendance rate is the clinic group's own figure.

That we caused all of it. The whole website is up 45% on bookings. Direct visits, which nobody buys, also booked more: 440 against 290. Some of the rise is the clinic group's own reputation and a better website, which we built, and some is demand we did not create.
That a UK clinic gets the same prices. This is a Norwegian account in Norwegian kroner. UK click prices in private healthcare are different, and usually higher.

Searches for the clinic's own name. Over half of the Google Ads bookings come from people who already knew C-Medical. We ran those campaigns, but we do not take credit for that demand. Without reception, bookings are up 15% and the cost per booking down 7%, not 28% and 13%.

The outpatient floor went backwards. Bookings for orthopaedics, dermatology and the other outpatient areas fell 29% once Performance Max was switched off. That was a choice: the campaign was buying brand searches and cheap, poorly qualified bookings.
The spring. From February to mid-May, the rebuilt account booked fewer patients than the old one had a year earlier. A rebuild has a learning period, and this one lasted about fourteen weeks.

Forty-two days are missing. A tracking fault from 13 July to 23 August 2026 hid bookings. Those days are removed from both years, so the comparison is fair, but the 2026 total is lower than the clinic group actually took.
Source: C-Medical's Google Ads account and Google Analytics 4 property, read through Windsor.ai on 5 November 2026. Published with the clinic group's written permission.
Window: 1 February to 5 November 2026 against the same calendar days of 2025. The 42 days of the tracking fault, 13 July to 23 August, are removed from both years, leaving 236 counted days.

Booking: the GA4 event booking_completed, a completed online booking. Google Ads bookings are those with source and medium google / cpc. Organic is any medium organic. AI search is chatgpt.com, perplexity, copilot, gemini.google.com and claude.ai. Google Ads' own conversion count is not used, because it counts some actions twice.
Treatment areas are derived from campaign names and have not been confirmed by the clinic group.
Currency: NOK converted at £1 = NOK 12.5148, the published rate for 5 November 2026. Kroner are the figures; pounds are for reading.

Revenue multiples use the clinic group's stated attendance (92%), first-consultation price (NOK 1,950) and average procedure value (NOK 59,000), and its stated range of 35% to 60% of consultations leading to a procedure.
